members.name: GetLinearVelocity
members.doc:
The character's OWN velocity. While grounded on a moving body the
ground's velocity at the contact (linear plus angular about it) is added
underneath for the step and the same share subtracted again here, so
gameplay reasons about walking speed relative to the platform; the
moment the feet leave it — a jump, the edge — the last ground velocity
stays folded in and the reported value becomes the world velocity the
character is carrying, and a landing re-bases that world velocity on
the new ground.

members.name: GetGroundVelocity
members.doc:
Velocity of whatever the character last stood on at the contact point,
zero while airborne or on static ground.

members.name: GetGroundSurface
members.doc:
Surface under the feet, taken from the ground contact Jolt already
tracks — no extra downward ray needed.

members.name: SetCrouched
members.doc:
Swap the capsule between standing and crouched height. Standing up is
refused (stays crouched) while an obstruction above would penetrate the
taller shape, and a changed heightScale re-shapes an already-crouched
capsule the same way. Returns the ACTUAL crouch state after the attempt.

members.name: GetShapeHeight
members.doc: Total capsule height currently applied (crouch shrinks it).

members.name: GetInnerBodyID
members.doc:
The kinematic body that gives the capsule presence in the broad phase.
Invalid when the component asked for no physical presence. PhysicsSystem
maps it back to the owning entity so a trace that strikes a character
resolves to an actor.

members.name: SetInnerBodyEnabled
members.doc:
Take the inner body out of / back into the simulation. A removed body
stops answering traces and contacts entirely — a disabled character must
not stay a wall. The BodyID (and its shape) survive.

members.name: SetPushFlags
members.doc:
Live push gating, so the details panel's flags take effect without
rebuilding the controller.

members.name: EntitySlotHint
members.doc:
The owning entity's ECS slot, cached for PhysicsSystem's per-frame
controller loops (World::GetComponentsHinted refreshes it in place).

types.name: FClothSkinnedSource
types.doc:
A skinned submesh handed to the cloth system by the layer that owns the
mesh (Physics cannot see the renderer's meshes or the animator). Positions
are the bind pose in mesh space; `indices` is the triangle list over
them; `boneIndices`/`boneWeights` are 4 per vertex; `maxDistance` is per
vertex (0 = hard-skinned).

types.name: FClothSkinPalette
types.doc:
The pose to skin against this frame: the animator's final skinning
palette (bind → posed, mesh space), the entity's world position and
rotation, and its uniform scale.

types.name: ClothSystem
types.doc:
Creates one Jolt soft body per Cloth entity (grid + XPBD edge/
shear/bend constraints from SoftBodySharedSettings::CreateConstraints),
mirrors world-space vertex bounds into the component every frame, and
removes the body when the component or entity goes away. Raw JPH types
stay inside Physics.dll (same rule as VehicleSystem).

members.name: GetVertexPositions
members.signature: bool GetVertexPositions(EntityID entity, std::vector<Vec3>& outPositions) const
members.doc:
World-space vertex positions (row-major, segmentsY rows of segmentsX).
False when the entity has no live cloth body yet.

members.name: FSkinnedSourceProvider
members.signature: using FSkinnedSourceProvider = std::function<bool(EntityID entity, int32_t submesh, FClothSkinnedSource& outSource)>
members.doc:
Skinned-mesh cloth. The providers are installed by the scene: the
source one answers once per cloth with the submesh's vertices, the
palette one every frame with the animator's pose. Vertices are
welded by position for the solver; GetSkinnedVertexPositions hands
back one MESH-SPACE position per ORIGINAL vertex, in the source's
order, so a render clone can be written straight from it.

Soft body over a static mesh: WORLD-space positions, one per original

types.name: ECollisionChannel
types.doc:
The channel a body identifies as (object channels) or a query traces against
(trace channels). Object channels describe what a collider IS; trace channels
describe a gameplay line-of-sight style query that is independent of physical
collision — a wall can block Visibility yet let a Projectile pass.

types.name: ECollisionPreset
types.doc: Named response sets a designer picks instead of authoring raw layer bits.

types.name: FCollisionResponseContainer
types.doc:
A body's object channel plus its per-channel response to every other channel.
Block/Overlap/Ignore mirror UE's per-channel model; ResolvePair collapses two
containers into the single response that governs a contact.

members.name: FromPreset
members.doc:
Build the response container a preset stands for. Custom returns a
block-everything container the caller then overrides field by field.

members.name: ResolvePair
members.signature: static ECollisionResponse ResolvePair(const FCollisionResponseContainer& a, const FCollisionResponseContainer& b)
members.doc:
Collapse two containers into the contact-governing response. Ignore if
either side ignores the other; Block only when each Blocks the other's
channel; Overlap for everything else (at least one Overlap, neither
Ignore) — an Overlap-vs-Block pair overlaps rather than blocking.

members.name: LayerForPreset
members.doc:
Map a preset onto the legacy object layer (ObjectLayers) so the
broad-phase matrix path keeps working underneath. Custom is
caller-defined (RigidBody.layer).

types.name: FCollisionMeshData
types.doc:
Triangle geometry pulled off a mesh asset for collision, in the asset's own
unscaled space. The cooked shape is scaled at body creation instead, so ten
crates at ten sizes still share one cooked mesh.

members.name: convexPieces
members.doc:
Authored convex pieces — the UCX_ sub-meshes an artist drew around the
model. When present, the SIMPLE collider is their union instead of one
hull swallowing the whole silhouette (the difference between a doorway
you can walk through and a solid block).

members.name: triangleSurfaces
members.doc:
What each triangle and each convex piece is MADE OF, taken from the
material bound to the submesh it came from. `triangleSurfaces` is either
empty or exactly indices.size() / 3 long; empty means no material on the
mesh authored a physics surface, so the whole shape answers with the
collider's own — which is what every mesh did before materials could
carry one.

members.name: dominantMaterial
members.doc:
The physics material of whichever bound material covers the most
triangles. A collider that names no `.physmat` of its own adopts it, so
"ice is slippery" is authored once on the material instead of retyped on
every collider placed on top of it. False means nothing authored one and
the collider keeps its inline values untouched.

members.name: authoredSetup
members.doc:
The mesh's own authored collision setup (`.mmeshmeta`) — the boxes,
spheres, capsules and generated hulls someone set up in the mesh editor,
plus which of the two channels they answer. It OUTRANKS both of the
fields above for simple collision: without it, "simple" meant one hull
swallowing the whole silhouette, which is why every prop in the engine
either collided as a 0.5m box or as its full render triangles.

members.name: cacheKey
members.doc:
Identity of the cooked result: the asset that produced it plus anything
that changes the geometry. Empty means "do not cache" — the geometry is
one-off and re-cooking it is the caller's business.

types.name: FCollisionMeshProvider
types.doc:
The seam that lets Physics cook collision from a mesh asset without reaching
up into Game: Game installs a resolver at image load, Physics calls it at
body creation. A null resolver simply means no mesh colliders resolve —
never a crash — which is also what a headless physics-only host wants.

types.name: FCollisionShapeCache
types.doc:
Cooked collision shapes shared by cache key. A triangle mesh costs multiple
megabytes and a measurable slice of level load to build; a hundred instances
of one prop must not each cook their own copy of it. Lookup and insertion
trade in Jolt shapes and live inside Physics (FCollisionShapeStore); this is
the part a tool or a test can drive.

members.name: Purge
members.doc:
Drops every cached shape. Shapes are refcounted, so bodies still
holding one keep it alive — this only releases the cache's reference.

members.name: maxSlopeAngle
members.doc: degrees

members.name: stepHeight
members.doc: Max step-up height

members.name: useGravity
members.doc: Auto-gravity (applied automatically in PhysicsSystem when not grounded)

members.name: layer
members.doc: Physics layer (0-31) for collision filtering

members.name: physicalPresence
members.doc:
A kinematic rigid body shaped like the capsule, carried along by the
controller. Without it the character exists ONLY inside its own sweep:
it is never added to the broad phase, so bullets, melee traces,
explosion overlaps, AI line-of-sight and the scanner all pass straight
through a player. Clear it only for a deliberately non-interactive
proxy (a spectator, a replay ghost).

members.name: pushBodies
members.doc:
Whether the character shoves dynamic bodies it walks into (bounded by
maxStrength), and whether moving bodies shove it back.

members.name: collisionPreset
members.doc:
Channel responses the inner body registers with, so a character answers
traces the same way a collider does. Preset seeds the whole set; the
overrides below apply when it is Custom.

members.name: controllerLive
members.doc:
Runtime state (managed by PhysicsSystem). The controller itself lives
in PhysicsSystem (GetCharacterController); this only says one is live.

members.name: netDriven
members.doc:
Stepped by its owner's network moves (FCharacterNetDriver on the
server), one step per move with that move's time, and never by the
frame: CharacterMovementSystem and the physics character pass skip it.

members.name: innerBodyID
members.doc:
The inner body Jolt created for the capsule. Invalid when
physicalPresence is off or body creation failed.

members.name: linearVelocity
members.doc:
The character's own velocity, relative to whatever it stands on. The
platform's share is carried separately in groundVelocity and folded
back in when the feet leave it, so a jump off a moving platform keeps
the platform's velocity.

members.name: groundVelocity
members.doc:
Velocity of the ground body at the contact point (linear plus angular
about the contact). Zero on static ground or in the air.

members.name: groundSurface
members.doc:
What the character is currently standing on. Jolt tracks the ground
contact's sub-shape, so this is the painted terrain layer or the struck
mesh triangle under the feet, not the whole body's material.

members.name: wantsCrouchShape
members.doc:
Crouch capsule request/state: gameplay (CharacterMovementSystem) sets
wantsCrouchShape; PhysicsSystem applies it each tick and reports back
the actual shape (standing up stays refused under a low ceiling).

types.name: EMovementMode
types.doc:
Custom hands the step to the function FCustomMovementModes holds under
CharacterMovementComponent::customMode.

members.name: maxJumpCount
members.doc: Jumps before landing (1 = no double jump). UE's JumpMaxCount.

members.name: jumpHoldTime
members.doc:
Variable jump height: while jump stays held, the jump keeps its launch
speed for up to this long. 0 = every jump is the same height. UE's
JumpMaxHoldTime.

members.name: coyoteTime
members.doc:
Coyote time: a ground jump is still allowed this long after walking off
a ledge.

members.name: useRootMotion
members.doc:
Root-motion locomotion: while walking, the animation's extracted root
delta (AnimatorComponent::rootMotionDeltaPosition, which needs
rootMotionEnabled on the animator) drives the capsule instead of the
input velocity. Input still steers facing/jump; horizontal speed comes
from the clip. Falls back to input velocity when no animator delta is
available.

members.name: rootMotionRotation
members.doc:
Also fold the root delta's yaw into the character's facing while
root-motion driven (turn-in-place / pivots authored in the clip).

members.name: customMode
members.doc: FCustomMovementModes id while mode == Custom.

members.name: jumpHeld
members.doc:
The jump button's level, not its edge: wantsJump is consumed by the
step that jumps, this stays true while the button is down and drives
jumpHoldTime.

members.name: rootMotionSources
members.doc:
Active root-motion sources, advanced by every movement step (so the
server's per-move step and the client's replay both run them).
Gameplay adds them with AddRootMotionSource.

members.name: inWater
members.doc:
Written by the Game-tier CharacterWaterSystem (the movement system in
Physics can't reach the water query directly): whether a water surface
covers the character, and how deep the FEET sit below it.

members.name: waterFlow
members.doc:
Downstream flow (m/s) of the covering water surface, written by the
Game-tier CharacterWaterSystem. Non-zero only inside a river body; the
swim branch adds it to the character's velocity so the current carries
the swimmer.

members.name: onLadder
members.doc:
Written by CharacterLadderSystem: whether a LadderVolume covers the
character and the world-space axis to climb along (normalized, usually
up). Swimming/Flying/Mantling take priority; otherwise entering a ladder
volume switches to Ladder mode and constrains motion to this axis.

members.name: ledgeDetected
members.doc:
Written by PhysicsSystem's ledge probe (previous frame's rays):
a mantleable ledge top in front of the character while airborne.

free.name: StepCharacterPlanarVelocity
free.signature: inline Vec3 StepCharacterPlanarVelocity(const Vec3& current, const Vec3& desired, bool grounded, const CharacterMovementComponent& mm, float dt)
free.doc:
The dt-correct planar (XZ) velocity step shared by CharacterMovementSystem,
the client's prediction replay and the server's pawn step — one formula, or
reconciliation fights the simulation. Grounded: friction redirects the
current velocity toward the input, maxAcceleration closes the speed gap,
and speed above the desired cap (sprint release, external launch) bleeds
off at brakingDeceleration instead of clamping in one frame. No input:
proportional friction plus constant braking, never through zero. Airborne:
acceleration scaled by airControl, capped so air input steers but never
gains speed beyond entry momentum or walk speed.

types.name: EClothSource
types.doc:
Where the cloth's vertices come from: a procedural grid at the entity,
or one submesh of the entity's skinned mesh, whose vertices follow the
skin and simulate within Max Distance of it.

types.name: ClothComponent
types.doc:
Cloth simulation on Jolt's XPBD soft body. The system builds a
horizontal segmentsX × segmentsY vertex grid at the entity's world
transform (local XZ plane), optionally pins the first row (the local
-Z edge), and lets Jolt's solver drape it against the world. Runtime
telemetry mirrors the world-space vertex bounds each frame; full
positions come from ClothSystem::GetVertexPositions (the future
render-mesh slice reads the same API).

members.name: stretchCompliance
members.doc: XPBD compliance: 0 = rigid distance constraints; larger = stretchier.

members.name: source
members.doc:
Skinned Mesh source: the submesh (0 = the primary) of this entity's
mesh renderer becomes the cloth. Every vertex of it is skinned by the
animator's pose each frame and may drift up to Max Distance from that
skinned position; 0 hard-skins it. With Mask From Vertex Color the red
channel scales the distance per vertex, so a painted collar stays put
while the hem swings. Grid fields (segments, width, length, pin) are
ignored for this source; mass, compliance, iterations and damping
apply to both.

members.name: pressure
members.doc:
Soft Body source: the submesh (a static mesh) becomes a free soft body
— a jelly, a cushion, a ball. Pressure inflates a closed mesh against
its own volume (0 = it slumps like cloth); edge stiffness comes from
the compliance fields above.

types.name: ColliderShape
types.doc: A single sub-shape within a compound collider

members.name: halfExtents
members.doc: Box

members.name: radius
members.doc: Sphere/Capsule

members.name: height
members.doc: Capsule

members.name: offset
members.doc: Local offset

members.name: staticBody
members.doc:
UE's default for a placed static mesh: collision on, simulation off. A
collider with no RigidBody used to be shape-without-body — the prop had
the right hull and nothing in the world could touch it — because
PhysicsSystem only ever built a body for entities carrying both. The
physics system now gives such a collider a static body of its own, and
takes it away the moment a RigidBody arrives to own the entity instead.
Turn this off for a collider that exists purely as authoring data (a
shape a tool will cook later, a proxy a gameplay system spawns from).

members.name: collisionPreset
members.doc:
UE-style collision channels. The preset picks a whole response set;
objectType and the response overrides below apply when preset == Custom.
Everything maps down to a Jolt object layer plus a response table the
contact filter consults, so the legacy layer/matrix path still works.

members.name: material
members.doc:
Physics material (per-collider friction/restitution).
The three fields surfaced via MOWO_NESTED match the legacy
mat_friction / mat_restitution / mat_density MDF keys exactly.

members.name: materialPath
members.doc:
A shared .physmat asset. When set it replaces the inline material
above wholesale at body creation, so "ice" is authored once and
referenced everywhere instead of retyped per collider.

members.name: surfaceType
members.doc:
What this collider is made of, for footsteps / impacts / decals / scans.
Ignored when materialPath resolves — the asset owns the surface then.

members.name: collisionMeshPath
members.doc:
Where a Mesh / ConvexHull collider's geometry comes from. Empty means
the entity's own MeshRenderer model, which is what "give this prop real
collision" means 95% of the time; point it at another asset for a
hand-authored low-poly proxy. Ignored when meshVertices is already
filled (terrain and the geometry tools cook their own).

members.name: materialSurfaces
members.doc:
Whether an asset-cooked shape stamps each triangle with the surface of
the material bound to the submesh it came from, and adopts that
material's friction and restitution when this collider names no
.physmat of its own. Turn it off for a proxy that is deliberately made
of one thing regardless of what the render mesh is painted with.

members.name: autoConvexCollision
members.doc:
Automatic convex decomposition for a ConvexHull collider whose mesh has
no authored simple collision and no UCX_ pieces. Off falls back to the
single hull over the whole silhouette, which is a solid block wherever
the mesh has a hole in it.

members.name: additionalShapes
members.doc: Additional shapes for compound collider (empty = single shape mode)

members.name: meshVertices
members.doc:
Mesh collider data (only used when shape == Mesh). Filled by whoever
cooks the geometry — terrain, the geometry tools, or the mesh-asset
resolver — and RELEASED once the shape is cooked and cached, because a
shared shape makes a per-collider copy of the triangle soup dead weight.

members.name: cookedShapeKey
members.doc:
Identity of the cooked shape in FCollisionShapeCache. Set by the
resolver; empty means this collider's geometry is one-off and must not
be shared with anything else.

members.name: assetGeometryFailureReported
members.doc:
Body creation retries every tick while a mesh collider's source asset is
not resident — which is what lets a proxy that streams in later still
cook. Without this latch the same two failure lines are written every
frame for the whole time it is missing, which buries everything else in
the log and reads as a hang.

members.name: meshTriangleSurfaces
members.doc:
One entry per triangle (meshIndices.size() / 3). Empty means the whole
mesh takes the material's surface. A wall whose lower band is stone and
whose upper band is wood is one mesh collider with two values here, and
a hit on it resolves to whichever triangle was actually struck.

members.name: heightfieldSamples
members.doc:
Height field data (only used when shape == HeightField). An n×n grid
of heights: world position of sample (i, j) is
heightfieldOffset + (i * scale.x, samples[j*n+i] * scale.y, j * scale.z).
Far more compact than an equivalent Mesh collider (terrain uses this).

members.name: heightfieldSurfaces
members.doc:
One entry per heightfield square, row-major over (n-1)x(n-1). Empty
means the whole field takes the material's surface. Terrain fills this
from the dominant painted layer so grass, rock and sand on one terrain
report as themselves.

types.name: EConstraintAxisMotion
types.doc:
Per-axis freedom of a 6DOF joint, UE's ELinearConstraintMotion /
EAngularConstraintMotion vocabulary.

types.name: EConstraintMotorMode
types.doc:
What a motor drives toward on its axis. Position holds an offset / angle;
Velocity keeps a rate (a turntable, a conveyor, a wheel).

members.name: connectedEntityId
members.doc:
Connected entity (the other body this constraint connects to). Handled
entirely by the custom (de)serialize hooks — needs MDF int64 round-trip
semantics that PropertyInfo's UUID type doesn't quite express.

members.name: anchorA
members.doc:
Anchor points relative to each body's centre of mass: A on this body, B
on the connected one. Both left at zero pins the joint at the bodies'
own centres; Fixed and Slider instead weld the bodies in their current
relative pose, which is the useful default for those two. Angles,
limits and motor targets all read as THIS body relative to the
connected one (or the world), whichever of the two it is attached to.

members.name: axisA
members.doc:
Axis (used by Hinge, Slider, and as the 6DOF joint's X axis), in the
same space as the anchors

members.name: hingeMotor
members.doc:
Hinge motor: Position holds hingeMotorTargetAngle, Velocity spins at
hingeMotorTargetVelocity. Re-applied every tick, so gameplay writing
the target is live.

members.name: springFrequency
members.doc: Spring settings (shared)

members.name: linearMotionX
members.doc:
SixDOF: per-axis freedom. Linear limits are symmetric half-ranges about
the anchor; angular limits are a min/max pair per axis, where X is the
twist about axisA and Y/Z the two swings (a pyramid, so each swing is
authored on its own). Defaults reproduce a ball socket.

members.name: linearMotorX
members.doc:
SixDOF motors, one per axis. Linear targets are in the connected body's
joint frame (axisB = X; the world's when unattached), angular targets in
this body's (axisA = X) — with the two axes authored alike, as they
usually are, the frames coincide at rest. Position targets are an
offset from the anchor / an Euler orientation; Velocity targets are
rates. Re-applied every tick like the hinge motor.

members.name: motorFrequency
members.doc:
Stiffness shared by every position motor, the hinge's included. For the
hinge and for each 6DOF angular axis the pair describes the swing about
the joint itself, however far the centre of mass sits from it. A
velocity motor ignores the spring and only honours the force / torque
cap.

members.name: breakForce
members.doc:
Break thresholds (0 = unbreakable), compared against the solver's
reaction each fixed step. Crossing either removes the joint, sets
`broken` and raises PhysicsSystem::OnConstraintBroken plus a
ConstraintBrokenEvent on the bus.

members.name: constraint
members.doc: Runtime state (managed by PhysicsSystem)

members.name: broken
members.doc:
Set when the break threshold fired. A broken joint is NOT rebuilt on the
next tick — before this flag existed the constraint re-formed one frame
after snapping. Clear it to re-form the joint deliberately.

types.name: LadderVolumeComponent
types.doc:
A climbable region. Placed as a box centered on the owning entity's
transform; a character whose feet fall inside it can enter Ladder movement
and climb along climbAxis (world space, usually up). CharacterLadderSystem
tests characters against every ladder volume each frame.

types.name: FPhysicalAnimationProfile
types.doc:
A per-bone-chain physical-animation profile: the motor gains that drive the
simulated bodies toward the animated pose. `strength` is the motor spring
frequency in Hz (higher = tracks the animation tighter, recovers faster),
`damping` its damping ratio. maxTorque caps the motor torque (0 = unlimited).

types.name: FPhysicalAnimationOverride
types.doc:
Motor gains for one sub-chain of the driven chain: the named bone plus
(when includeChildren) its descendants take these instead of the component
profile. Overrides apply in order, so a broad spine entry can be narrowed by
a later one on a hand — without that, a spine stiff enough to carry a hit
reaction also welds the fingers.

types.name: PhysicalAnimationComponent
types.doc:
Blends simulated physics onto an animated skeleton over a bone chain — hit
reactions that recover. The named chain root plus (optionally) its
descendants are simulated as a powered ragdoll: motors pull the bodies
toward the animated pose while gameplay impulses knock them off it, and the
physics contribution blends back to animation over `recoverTime`.

Lifecycle (managed by PhysicalAnimationSystem):
- enabled=false        → dormant, pure Animator playback
- continuous=true      → the chain is always physically driven at
blendWeight (floppy hair, a limp arm)
- continuous=false     → the chain rides the animation exactly until an
impulse lands; then physics takes over at
blendWeight and decays back over recoverTime

types.name: PhysicalAnimationComponent::PendingImpulse

types.name: RagdollMode
types.doc:
Drives a character's animated skeleton with a physics ragdoll.

Lifecycle (managed by RagdollSystem):
- `enabled = false`           → no physics, normal Animator playback
- `enabled = true, mode = …`  → on the next tick the system materializes
a ragdoll from the entity's
AnimatorComponent::skeleton, snaps the
bodies to the current animated pose,
and starts simulating
- `enabled = false` after on  → system removes the bodies and the
Animator takes over again next frame

Mode semantics:
- Animated  — physics off, this component is dormant
- Ragdoll   — physics fully drives the skeleton; AnimationSystem still
ticks clips so we can blend back later, but boneMatrices
are overwritten from body poses each frame
- Hybrid    — blended weight between animated and physics
(per-bone weight curve, head/upper-body driven anim
while lower-body ragdolls, etc.)

types.name: RagdollBoneOverride
types.doc:
Per-bone tweaks applied on top of the auto-rig defaults. All fields are
multiplicative / delta-style (massScale = 1.0 means "use builder
default"; swingDeg = 0 means "use builder default 45°"). Designers
override sparsely — typical use: bulk up the head, tighten the elbow
twist, soften the spine swing. Only entries actually present in the
vector get applied; bones without an override use auto-rig defaults.

members.name: currentBlend
members.doc:
Blend tween state. `current` is the visual weight applied to the
animation→physics lerp this frame; it walks toward `target` at a
rate derived from blendInTime/blendOutTime. The teardown threshold
is current ≤ 1e-3 (any positive value still needs physics around for
the lerp to produce a meaningful pose).

types.name: RagdollComponent::PendingImpulse
types.doc:
Queued hit-reaction impulses. Gameplay code calls
Ragdoll.ApplyImpulse / ApplyImpulseAtBone / EnablePhysics(impulse,
point) and the request lands here. RagdollSystem drains the queue
each tick AFTER making sure the ragdoll is materialized — so calling
`EnablePhysics(impulse, point)` on an entity that doesn't have a
live ragdoll yet still works: the ragdoll is built on the same tick
and the impulse fires on the freshly-spawned body. boneIndex == -1
means "apply on the pelvis"; any other value targets that bone's
body (resolved through `mappings`). hasPoint=false → at center-of-
mass (fastest path, behaves like RigidBody.AddImpulse).

the child entity whose transform the system writes every tick, so a wheel

types.name: PhysicalAnimationSystem
types.doc:
Drives a bone chain with motor-powered physics blended onto the animated
pose, so hit reactions knock a limb off the animation and then recover.

Tick order: runs AFTER PhysicsSystem (bodies already stepped this frame) and
AFTER AnimationSystem (boneMatrices carry the animated pose). It drives the
motors toward the just-computed animated pose, reads the stepped bodies back,
and blends them into the chain's bones by the current physics weight. Because
the sim is fixed-step (1/60) and this runs post-step, the readback samples a
settled pose and the motor targets set here take effect on the next step.

Later overrides win on overlap, so a broad entry can be narrowed by a
deeper one. Bones outside the driven chain get an entry too — the caller
only reads the driven ones. Pure — no physics, CPU-testable.

Which motion types a query is allowed to see. DynamicOnly covers everything

The swept / overlapped volume. Primitives only: the shape is built per call,

types.name: FQueryFilter
types.doc:
Everything a query filters on, in one place. The legacy entry points took a
layer mask and a single ignored body, which is why a scanner could not skip
its own carrier plus the prop in its hands, and why "by channel" only
existed for plain rays.

members.name: channel
members.doc:
A body participates only when its registered response to this channel is
Block — or Overlap, when includeOverlaps is set on a multi query. Bodies
with no registered response Block, so externally created geometry still
stops traces.

members.name: useChannel
members.doc:
Off = the object-layer mask path instead, for callers that reason in
layers. layerMask is ignored while useChannel is on.

members.name: includeOverlaps
members.doc:
Multi queries only: report the bodies the trace passed through as
Overlap hits alongside the blocking one, the way UE's multi traces do.

members.name: ignoreSensors
members.doc:
A sensor body is a gameplay volume; stopping a bullet on a trigger box
is almost never what the caller meant.

members.name: ignoreBodies
members.doc:
Bodies dropped from the result set — the shooter's own capsule, the
carried prop, everything a penetrating shot has already passed.

members.name: subShapeID
members.doc:
Identifies the exact triangle / heightfield square / compound leaf that
was struck, for a later surface or material re-resolve.

members.doc:
The gameplay entity behind the body, resolved on the query path so a
caller does not need a second map lookup per hit. INVALID_ENTITY for
bodies nobody registered (raw physics bodies, ragdoll parts).

members.name: shapeCenter
members.doc:
Sweeps only: where the swept shape's centre sat at impact. Rays leave it
equal to location.

members.name: response
members.doc:
Block for the hit that stopped the trace, Overlap for a body the trace
only reported on its way through.

types.doc:

construction, the narrow-phase lookup and the job dispatch ONCE for the
whole sweep instead of once per ray, and the rays fan out across the worker
pool. Fill, Execute, read; the storage is reused across frames, so a
per-frame scanner allocates nothing after its first sweep.

narrow phase, which must not be mid-step. Results line up index for
index with the Add calls.

Below this many rays the batch runs inline — the dispatch costs more

members.doc:
Estimated normal impulse of the impact (kg m/s); zero on stay events,
sensors and overlaps. Equal for both sides of the pair.

members.doc:
Simulation time the substep cap (p.MaxSubsteps) refused to run, and how
many frames hit the cap. Both stay zero on a healthy frame budget.

members.name: GetAsyncStepsInFlight

members.doc:
p.OverlapDuringPhysics (on by default): UE's StartPhysics / EndPhysics. The
scene kicks the frame's steps onto a worker after the PrePhysics tick
group, ticks DuringPhysics while Jolt runs, then joins — instead of the
step running inside Update with the game thread waiting. EndFrameStep
runs Update's post-step half, so the Update that follows in the same
frame does nothing. BeginFrameStep returns false (Update does it all)
when the overlap is off or p.AsyncTick owns the step. The scene runs
the world systems ordered ahead of this one (World::UpdateBefore)
before the kick, so movement input still lands on this frame's step.

members.name: OnConstraintBroken
members.doc:
Raised the fixed step a ConstraintComponent crossed its break threshold,
after the joint is gone and `broken` is set. The same payload rides the
EventBus as ConstraintBrokenEvent for listeners that never see this
system (audio, VFX, replication).

members.name: SetSimulationFocus
members.doc:
Simulation LOD: dynamic bodies beyond the sleep radius around
the focus are force-deactivated; they wake when the focus comes back
within the (smaller) wake radius. No focus = no LOD. Radii override
via p.LODSleepRadius / p.LODWakeRadius, kill switch via p.LOD.

members.name: GetLodFrozenCount
members.doc:
Bodies currently frozen by the simulation LOD. Diagnostic (and the
self-tests pin that destroyed entities don't linger here).

members.name: GetLodBodiesExaminedLastUpdate
members.doc:
Bodies the last LOD pass looked at: the active ones, plus the frozen set
on a frame the focus moved. Diagnostic — a settled world reads zero.

members.name: ShiftOrigin
members.doc:
Origin rebasing: translate every Jolt body and character
controller by -shift, velocities untouched. Callers (Scene) shift
the transform components; this keeps the physics mirror aligned.

members.name: StepCharacter
members.doc:
Advance ONE character controller by dt outside the fixed-step loop:
integrates gravity into the component's linearVelocity, runs the Jolt
ExtendedUpdate against the live collision world, and writes the result
back to the component + transform. Game-thread only, never while
Update is running — the client-prediction replay path steps a rewound
character through the still-unacked inputs with this.

members.name: SetCharacterPosition
members.signature: bool SetCharacterPosition(uint64_t entityId, const Vec3& position)
members.doc:
Teleport a character controller (and its transform) — the rewind half
of the prediction reconcile.

members.name: GetCharacterController
members.doc:
The live controller behind an entity, nullptr when none — diagnostics
and the self-tests (capsule shape state isn't mirrored on the component).

members.name: GetQueryBodyForEntity
members.doc:
The body a query originating ON this entity must exclude: its rigid body
if it has one, otherwise its character controller's inner body. Looking
up RigidBodyComponent alone misses characters entirely, and a ray that
starts inside a convex shape reports a hit at fraction 0 — which is how
an AI standing in its own capsule goes blind, or a foot-IK probe lands on
its own knee. Anything tracing from a pawn wants this, not the component.

members.name: GetEntityForBody
members.doc: Look up EntityID for a physics body (returns INVALID_ENTITY if not found)

members.name: GetRegisteredBodyCount
members.doc:
Bodies this system has registered — RigidBody bodies, character inner
bodies and implicit statics alike. Diagnostic, and the self-tests read it
to pin that a torn-down entity leaves nothing behind.

members.signature: bool GetBodyInterpolation(uint64_t entityId, FBodyInterp& out) const

members.name: OnCollisionEnterEvents
members.doc:
The single-slot callbacks above belong to whichever system claimed them
(the interactable system owns collision enter). Anything else that wants
contact begins — an actor's OnHit event — subscribes here and is told
about the same pairs, once per side, after the slot callback ran.

members.name: GetImplicitStaticBody
members.doc:
The static body this system created for a collider that carries no
RigidBody, if any. Diagnostics and the self-tests — nothing is stored on
the component, because the body is derived state and must not survive a
save/load round trip as authored data.

members.name: GetImplicitStaticPoseReadCount
members.doc:
How many times an implicit static's world pose has been re-derived from
its transform since the system started. Diagnostic — a frame in which no
prop's transform was rebuilt adds nothing.

types.name: PhysicsSystem::FBodyInterp
types.doc:
Physics→render interpolation: the fixed-step sim advances in
1/60 chunks while the frame time is variable, so dynamic bodies would
judder at any refresh ≠ 60. Every dynamic body keeps its previous and
current physics transform; SyncFromPhysics writes the render transform
as a lerp/slerp between them by alpha = accumulator / fixedTimestep.
The simulation itself is untouched — only the rendered pose is
interpolated. Kinematic/static bodies and character controllers are
authoritative and never interpolated.

members.name: active
members.doc:
Captured with the poses so SyncFromPhysics never asks Jolt — under
the async tick Jolt may be mid-step when the render pose is written.

types.name: PhysicsSystem::FImplicitStaticBody
types.doc:
A body this system owns on behalf of a collider whose entity carries no
RigidBody — UE's implicit static: collision enabled, simulation off.
The pose and the shape identity are kept so a prop dragged in the editor
takes its collision with it (a static body never moves on its own, so
nothing else would notice) and a reshaped collider is rebuilt.

members.name: numThreads
members.doc:
Upper bound on the workers Jolt splits a phase across (-1 = the whole
engine pool). Caps the split only; no engine worker is spawned or parked.

members.name: singleThreadedJobs
members.doc:
Escape hatch: run Jolt's jobs on the stepping thread instead of the
engine worker pool. Off everywhere by default; flip it if a platform
bring-up ever hits pool trouble mid-port.

members.name: deterministic
members.doc:
Reproducible mode (p.Deterministic): Jolt's jobs run on the stepping
thread in a fixed order whatever numThreads says, and contact events are
handed to gameplay sorted by body pair rather than in worker-completion
order. Jolt's own guarantee — same binary, same CPU, same inputs, same
results — is what this mode makes the ENGINE honour on top; without it
the step is still Jolt-deterministic but the event order is not.

members.name: subShapeID
members.doc:
Identifies the exact triangle / heightfield square / compound leaf that
was struck. Keep it if you want to re-resolve the surface later.

members.name: point
members.doc:
The impact point ON the struck surface — for shape casts this is the
contact point, not the swept shape's center (decals, impact FX and the
camera boom all want the surface).

members.name: normal
members.doc: Points OUT of the struck surface, toward the query.

members.name: shapeCenter
members.doc:
Shape casts only: where the swept shape's center was at the time of
impact (origin + dir * fraction). Raycasts leave it equal to `point`.

members.name: surface
members.doc:
Resolved from the sub-shape, so a mesh with per-triangle surfaces or a
terrain with painted layers answers per hit rather than per body.

types.name: FPhysicsBodyDesc
types.doc:
A primitive body created straight through the world, outside any component
(preview floors, tool geometry, tests). `extents` follows EQueryShape: a
sphere reads x as the radius, a box all three as half extents, a capsule x
as the radius and y as the half height of the cylinder.

members.name: mass
members.doc: Above zero overrides the mass (inertia still follows the shape).

members.name: linearDamping
members.doc: Negative keeps Jolt's default damping.

members.name: StepAsync
members.doc:
The async tick (p.AsyncTick). StepAsync hands `stepCount` fixed steps to
the worker pool and returns at once; WaitForStep joins them. Between the
two, Jolt belongs to the job: every entry point below that reaches it
joins first (counted in GetAsyncJoinStalls, so a project can see which
caller keeps forfeiting the overlap), and the only read surface that
does not wait is what PhysicsSystem copied out at the previous join —
transforms, the interpolation snapshot, the character components, the
contact events. The persistent-load channel is safe to write throughout:
the job consumes the copy it was handed at submit.

members.doc:
Physics-internal: the Jolt side of this world, joined first like every
other entry point. The type is only complete inside the Physics module.

members.name: SetPersistentForce
members.doc:
Persistent per-body force/torque channel. Jolt clears accumulated
forces after every Update, so a force applied once per frame reaches
only the FIRST substep of a multi-substep frame — everything after it
integrates force-free. Loads registered here are re-applied at the top
of every Step, making the effect substep-count independent. The channel
is re-armed each frame: PhysicsSystem clears it after its substep loop,
so per-frame sources (buoyancy, wind) just Add every tick. Direct
PhysicsWorld steppers own the clearing themselves. One-shot impulses
stay on AddImpulse.

get the body's uniform surface. This is the single resolution path — the

types.name: RagdollSystem
types.doc:
Owns the lifecycle of every active physics ragdoll in the World and
each frame reads the simulated body transforms back into the owning
entity's AnimatorComponent::boneMatrices so the skinned mesh renders
the physics-driven pose.

Tick order: ragdoll bodies are activated by Jolt during PhysicsSystem
step. RagdollSystem::Update runs AFTER PhysicsSystem::Update (registered
later in Scene system init) and AFTER AnimationSystem so its writes to
boneMatrices are not overwritten by FK. The skinning shader picks up
whatever's there at the end of the frame.

types.name: ESurfaceType
types.doc:
What a surface is made of, as far as gameplay is concerned. This is the one
authored answer to "what am I standing on / what did I just hit", shared by
footstep audio, impact VFX, decals and the scanner's point colouring.

It is carried by the physics material rather than the render material: a
contact and a query both land on a collider, so keying off physics means the
answer is authored once and is reachable from every hit without a second
lookup through the renderer. Values serialize by name, so inserting an entry
does not invalidate existing content.

members.name: ScanColor
members.doc:
The colour a scanner paints a point when its ray lands on this surface,
packed RGBA8 as r | g<<8 | b<<16 | a<<24 — the point-cloud vertex layout.
Keying the palette off the physics surface is the whole reason the
surface lives on the collider: a ray already knows what it hit, so the
colour needs no second lookup through the render material.

The wheels a component simulates: its authored list, or the legacy
four-wheel layout synthesized from the scalar fields when the list is
empty. Pure, so the layout contract is pinnable without Jolt.

members.name: PairDrivenWheels
members.signature: static std::vector<std::pair<int32_t, int32_t>> PairDrivenWheels(const std::vector<FVehicleWheelSetup>& wheels)
members.doc:
Driven wheels paired into differentials: wheels on one axle (same z
within a tolerance) pair left/right, a lone driven wheel gets a
one-sided differential. Jolt takes -1 for the missing side.
